title: Atlas Bank: Model Onboarding Playbook & Regression Checklist (PII datasets)
summary: Customer-specific onboarding pack for Atlas Bank. Contains pinned prompts, private dataset inventory and handling notes, detailed acceptance criteria for model quality and safety, and a step-by-step regression + sign-off checklist to hand off to SRE/Product/Security.
model_target: instruction-tuned 7B variant (quantized 4-bit) for sensitive banking assistant tasks: transaction summarization, intent classification, PII redaction guidance, and short-form compliance explanations.
objective: Provide a deterministic acceptance path so the Atlas Bank product team can deploy an inference-backed assistant that meets quality, latency, and privacy constraints. We prioritize low hallucination on entity-heavy prompts and strict PII handling.
private_datasets: atlas_txn_q1_2024_redacted.csv - 18.6k rows, transaction-level labels (intent, merchant-category), PII tokenized with redaction-map v2
atlas_customer_faq_2023_parsed.jsonl - 4.2k Q/A pairs extracted from Atlas internal KB (sensitive entries flagged)
atlas_regulatory_snippets.txt - curated excerpts for compliance checks (200 doc snippets)
atlas_human_eval_bundle_2025-01.zip - 1k human-annotated summaries and hallucination flags (stored on secure bucket, access via internal helpdesk)
pinned_prompts:
Prompt A - transaction summarization (short): 

"You are an internal compliance reviewer. Summarize the transaction below in 2-3 bullets highlighting: merchant, amount, unusual indicators (if any), and whether additional review is recommended. Do NOT infer any PII beyond the fields provided.

Transaction: [RAW_TRANSACTION_PAYLOAD]"

Prompt B - intent classification (multi-label): 

"Classify the customer message into the following labels: [payment_issue, chargeback_request, merchant_dispute, account_update, other]. Return a JSON list of labels only. If uncertain, return ["other"]."

Prompt C - PII redaction guidance (agent): 

"Given the text below, return a redacted version where account numbers, SSNs, and full names are replaced with <REDACTED_TYPE>. Keep other contextual info intact and add a one-line rationale explaining each redaction.

Text: [CUSTOMER_MESSAGE]"
baseline_metrics: P95 latency (staging dedicated GPU) for 512-token gen: 340ms
acceptance_criteria: Intent classification: macro-F1 >= 0.88 on atlas_labelset_v2 (n >= 4,500; stratified by merchant class)
Summarization: human-checked accuracy >= 90% for required fields (merchant, amount, recommendation) on a 1,000-sample spot-check
Hallucination: entity-hallucination <= 0.6% measured on 1,000 entity-bearing queries (human adjudicated)
PII redaction: automated redaction precision >= 99.5% and recall >= 98% compared to redaction-map v2
Latency: p95 <= 400ms on dedicated-staging cluster with production-like load (2k rps simulated burst test)
Regression: no statistically significant drop (p < 0.01) on any primary metric vs baseline model (two-sided t-test where applicable)
Security/Privacy: model must pass the internal privacy scan (no dataset leakage flags) and the external vulnerability checklist from security team
Cost: amortized token cost per 1k tokens <= $1.30 under expected batching profile
regression_test_suite: Data sanity: run dataset validation (scripts/validate_private_datasets.sh) to assert schema, label coverage, and PII tokenization preserved
Automated evals: run evaluation harness on atlas_labelset_v2 and human_eval_bundle; capture metrics and diffs
A/B comparison: evaluate candidate vs baseline for intent F1, summarization ROUGE-L, hallucination; store per-example diffs for manual review (top 200 regressions)
Stress test: 10-minute burst at 2k rps on dedicated-staging to measure latency tail and error rate; collect allocator traces
Privacy regression: run redaction-regression tool and compare to redaction-map v2; surface false negative cases for triage
Fallback validation: force model-variant fallback (simulate capacity loss) and confirm downstream app returns degrade-gracefully message as per rollout policy
Human-in-the-loop spot check: sample 300 examples across intents and merchant classes; label with hallucination flag and summary correctness
Embedding drift: compute mean cosine similarity against baseline embeddings for 5k sample queries; drift threshold <= 0.02
signoff_steps: Applied ML lead (Maya Rodriguez) verifies automated evals and per-example regression triage completed and uploads results to Confluence page
SRE (Arman Gupta) approves performance & p95 latency SLOs on staging-dedicated run
Security & Privacy (Priya Patel) signs off on privacy scan and dataset access logs; confirms KMS integration for keys used in private bucket
Product (Atlas Bank contact + Redwood CSM) confirms business acceptance for edge cases and approves canary rollout plan
Legal/Compliance signs off on retention and data handling appendix before private deployment
deployment_notes: Canary rollout plan: 5% traffic for 72 hours -> 25% for 48 hours -> 100% when no regression alarms. Fallback variant: quantized 3B that has lower cost but higher hallucination; automatic rollback threshold: any metric breach in acceptance_criteria or >0.5% error-rate increase.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: PII redaction misses structured account numbers in free-text uploads. Mitigation: add regex-based pre-scan and escalate flagged examples to manual redaction queue. Risk: embedding drift on merchant-names causing rerank drops; Mitigation: add embedding anchoring examples and monitor cosine similarity daily.
next_steps: 1) Lock dataset access perms and request security audit (ticket ML-4213). 2) Run full regression harness and circulate diff_report.html to stakeholders. 3) Schedule 1-hour walkthrough with Atlas product + compliance for signoff.
notes: This document is a working playbook. Expect iterative updates after first canary. Store all raw evaluation outputs in secure bucket 's3://redwood-evals/atlas-bank/2025-01-10/' and attach checksums to Confluence page. If questions, ping #applied-ml and tag @maya.
